approved: Foreign Acquisitions and Takeovers Amendment (Strategic Assets) Bill 2016
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would stop foreign individuals and companies from buying a 10% or larger share of Australian land, water, or other assets considered vital to the economy or defence.
A new body called the Foreign Ownership Assessment Board would decide which assets count as strategically important, with its membership set by a Senate majority.
A foreign entity could still acquire up to a 45% interest if both houses of Parliament approve it by a two-thirds majority vote.
Creates a Foreign Ownership Assessment Board to classify assets as strategically important.
Bans foreign acquisitions of a 10% or greater interest in assets deemed strategically important, unless Parliament overrides the ban.
Allows appeals of Board decisions to a Tribunal and then to a court.
Foreign persons and entities seeking to acquire interests in Australian land, water, or other assets of strategic importance.
